messages:
mia: Quick thread — I'm kicking off an adaptive delay-cap probe for continuous batching across three tenant classes (free / standard / premium). Goal: quantify tail latency, throughput, and inter-tenant fairness when kernel selection falls back (fp16 -> int8 -> generic) and when KV cache hotkeys shift. Kicking off in the staging harness now.

raj: Nice. Which harness mix are you using? Pure synthetic, replay, or a hybrid? Need consistent generator so comparisons are valid.

mia: Hybrid — 70% synthetic Poisson bursts (to hit microbursts) + 30% replayed session traces from last week's canary. Trying to avoid model-version drift; pinned to commit rfd-2026-03-12.

lee: Make sure to pin kernel flags too (autotune off) so we don't get noise from background kernel selection. Also record the selected kernel per request in the trace.

emily: Early note: KV cache behavior will dominate if prefixes are skewed. For the hybrid run, recommend three prefix distributions: uniform, hotspot (5% keys = 50% traffic), and churn (new keys ramp). That'll exercise cache thrash.

sam: Ran a 10m smoke with batch_cap=64 and max_delay_ms=8. Observed premium tenants had stable p95 ~28ms, standard ~42ms, free spiked to p95 180ms during bursts. Looks like delay-budget fairness is wrong — free got deprioritized by queueing policy.

perf-bot: PROFILE SUMMARY (run 1804202501):
- kernel_fallback_rate: fp16=62%, int8=28%, generic=10%
- 99th latency increased +12% when max_delay_ms increased from 2->8 (burst window)
- KV hit rate: uniform=78%, hotspot=41%, churn=22%
- CPU sidewall clock: kernel selection overhead ~0.7ms/request when fallback to generic

mia: Oof. That generic fallback + high batch_delay is the combo killing tails. Hypothesis: queueing allows large batches to form for free tenant; runtime then picks generic kernel for wide seq lengths -> long exec time -> head-of-line blocking.

raj: Two quick actions: 1) enforce per-tenant max_batch_size (smaller for free), 2) cap the max_delay dynamically based on current kernel profile (if generic usage > 5% reduce delay). Want to try heuristics A and B.

emily: Also test per-tenant KV partitions (soft isolation) to avoid hotkey thrash affecting premium. If that reduces cross-tenant variance, it's promising.

lee: I'll add instrumentation to emit per-tenant chosen_kernel and per-batch seq stats. Keep autotune disabled for the runs.

mia: Plan for next 24h: run baseline (current prod cfg) + heurA (per-tenant batch cap) + heurB (dynamic delay cap) across the three prefix distributions. Collect p50/p95/p99, kernel mix, kv hit, and fairness delta (p95_premium - p95_free).

sam: I'll schedule the runs and drop logs into /staging/perf/180420. Will post summary when done.

mia: Thanks — if we see heurB reduce p99 tails without dropping throughput we can roll to canary. If heurA is simpler and wins, that might be safer for immediate mitigation.

perf-bot: ACTION: job scheduled (id perf-180420-01). Expected finish ~2h.

mia: Great. Keep notes short here; paste CSVs or quick plots into the thread when ready. :rocket:
